purpose: Reconciled source purposes: [1] Define qc analysis target locality explicitly so quality/code analysis can be run against local or declared external sources without conflating external transport reachability with semantic authority. [2] Define explicit QC analysis locality so local and external analysis backends/sources are selectable without changing the semantic identity of the analysis target.

owns: QC Local and External Mode semantics

value.authorization_rule: External reachability does not grant target read/write authority.
value.external_rule: Reconciled source clauses: [1] External mode requires an explicit external identity/reference and governed access path. [2] External mode uses an explicitly governed external backend/service/source path.
value.fallback_rule: Local/external fallback is explicit; failure never silently changes locality.
value.local_rule: Reconciled source clauses: [1] Local mode resolves qc target inside the local owned/available semantic or source boundary. [2] Local mode uses configured local backend/resources.
value.mode_rule: QC locality is explicit per invocation/profile.
value.privacy_rule: External mode requires explicit data/export/privacy policy satisfaction before sending context.
value.provenance_rule: Reconciled source clauses: [1] qc output retains local/external target provenance. [2] Result records mode, backend and source refs.
value.read_rule: External read access does not imply external write authority.
value.selection_rule: Mode is explicit in invocation/configuration; it is not inferred from URL-looking strings or network reachability alone.
value.target_rule: Analysis target identity is independent from local/external execution locality.
value.transport_rule: Transport endpoint is binding only and not external semantic target identity.
value.write_rule: Any external mutation requires an explicit supported write operation and remote authorization.

invariants.rule: q-family roles, backend aliases, targets, command namespaces and help metadata remain explicit and do not derive authority from model/backend output.
q/qc/qt model execution produces inert candidate data; models may request or propose operations but only AIGMos canonical validation, authorization and dispatch can create effects.

references.purpose: External qc access uses governed remote semantics where applicable.
External targets remain explicit external identities.
QC mode remains separate from target identity.
